title: ONEXUS Graph Data
description: Data format accepted by ONEXUS (https://github.com/) for loading a graph — a network of nodes (elements: components, spaces, organizations, vendors, systems...) connected by typed, directional edges (relationships). Give this schema to an AI assistant along with your own data (a spreadsheet, a list, a database export, anything) and ask it to convert your data into a JSON file that validates against this schema. Only `elements` is strictly required; everything else has sensible defaults or is optional metadata. Fields not described here are still allowed and preserved — ONEXUS plugins may read extra fields you add.

meta.description: Optional project-level metadata. Not required to load, but recommended.

schema.description: Version tag for this data format. Use "onexus-1.1" unless told otherwise.

project.description: Human-readable name of the project or dataset this graph represents.

timestamp.description: When this data was generated or exported, ISO 8601.

phases.description: Ordered list of lifecycle phase names used anywhere in this graph's edges (e.g. project stages, workflow steps). Free-form — invent names that fit your domain.

languageDefault.description: Which language of each node's `label` to display by default. Only "en" and "jp" are actually rendered by ONEXUS today.

elements.description: The graph itself: a list of nodes and a list of edges connecting them.

nodes.description: Every entity in the graph — a physical component, a space, an organization, a vendor, a system, anything you want to model as a 'thing'.

edges.description: Every relationship between two nodes, referenced by their `id`.

label.description: Display name of a node, keyed by language. Only `en` and `jp` are stored and rendered by ONEXUS — other language keys you add will be dropped when the file is loaded.

jp.description: Japanese display name. Optional — falls back to `en` if omitted.

node.description: One graph node, wrapped in a `data` object (this mirrors the Cytoscape.js element format ONEXUS is built on).

id.description: Unique identifier for this node within the graph. Referenced by edges' `source`/`target`. Must be unique across all nodes.

nodeType.description: Broad kind of thing this node represents. Free-form, but these values get distinct icons/styling in ONEXUS: "Component" (the default if omitted or unrecognized), "System", "Space", "Organization", "Vendor", "ComponentType", "PropertySet", "Port", "Option", "Tag". Any other value is accepted and just renders as a generic node.

category.description: Finer-grained classification within `nodeType`, used for coloring/grouping and the legend (e.g. "Door", "SecurityDevice", "DesignTeam"). Free-form — invent categories that fit your domain. Either `category` or `revitCategory` must be present.

revitCategory.description: Autodesk Revit category name, if this node originated from a Revit model (e.g. "Doors", "Electrical Equipment"). Used as a fallback for `category` when `category` is omitted. Either `category` or `revitCategory` must be present.

level.description: Optional building level / floor this node belongs to (e.g. "Level 1"). Purely descriptive metadata.

edge.description: One directed or undirected relationship between two nodes, wrapped in a `data` object.

id.description: Unique identifier for this edge within the graph.

type.description: Name of the relationship (e.g. "Controls", "Supplies", "LocatedIn", "DesignedBy"). Free-form — this is the label shown on the edge and in the legend.

dimension.description: Which semantic category of relationship this is, used to group edges in the legend and for filtering. Free-form, but ONEXUS suggests these starter values: "System", "Spatial", "Responsibility", "Vendor". Any other string works fine and just becomes a new legend group.

source.description: `id` of the node this edge starts from. Must match an existing node's `id`.

target.description: `id` of the node this edge points to. Must match an existing node's `id`.

directional.description: Whether this edge has a direction (drawn with an arrowhead) or represents a symmetric relationship (drawn without one).

phase.description: Which project phase(s) this relationship is active/relevant in (e.g. ["Design", "Construction"]). Free-form — should match names used in `meta.phases`.

owner.description: Who is responsible for this relationship (a discipline, team, or role name). Purely descriptive metadata.

risk.description: Risk level of this relationship, used by the Risk layer to color and size edges. Use "High"/"Medium"/"Low" — ONEXUS also accepts lowercase or single-letter ("h"/"m"/"l") or numeric (1-3 or a raw 0-1 score) variants, but the three values here are the canonical form to generate.

confidence.description: How certain this relationship is. "Inferred" renders as a dashed edge (lower confidence, e.g. derived or assumed); "Explicit" (or any other/omitted value) renders as a normal solid edge.

notes.description: Free-text explanation of this relationship, shown in the detail panel.

relationshipContract.description: Optional canonical relationship envelope. Legacy ONEXUS 1.x edge fields remain valid and are normalized into this structure at load time.

truthClass.description: How this relationship became accepted. Inferred relationships remain proposals until explicitly reviewed and promoted.

system.description: Originating system or adapter, such as Autodesk ACC, OneRoot, Revit, or CSV.

recordId.description: Stable relationship identifier in the originating system.

url.description: Deep link to the authoritative source item when available.

method.description: How the relationship was obtained, for example import, API, rule, inference, or human capture.

confidence.description: Confidence label or numeric score supplied by the source or inference process.

data.notes: Door is part of the access control system.
